strategy.summary: Reproduce pandas PR 62582 by building the buggy commit 25607882c53f from source (editable meson build with Cython), applying the developer's test_ints.py diff, and running the C-engine overflow tests. On the buggy revision the c-engine overflow tests fail because big integers come back as strings; on the fixed revision they pass. The test compares exact integers, so no numeric tolerance is involved. The environment (NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata, Cython) has no documented version constraint in the evidence, so the versions chosen below are inferred from the pinned build requirements of the checked-out revision, not from documentation.

system_packages: ninja-build (only if meson requires it on this platform)
pinned_because: NumPy: no documented constraint in evidence, so use the version listed in pandas' pyproject.toml build-system/runtime requirements for this revision (era-inferred from the checked-out tree, not documented); it is numerically relevant only for the object-dtype construction path
Cython: no documented constraint; use the version pyproject.toml pins for the build backend at this revision, since the C parser .pyx must be regenerated from source
python-dateutil and tzdata: documented but not numerically relevant; left at the versions the pandas install resolves, not pinned
Python interpreter: not stated in evidence; choose a version the checked-out pyproject.toml declares as supported, and record it

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest pandas/tests/io/parser/common/test_ints.py -k 'int64_overflow or int64_uint64_range or outside_int64_uint64_range' -q -p no:cacheprovider
strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/io/parser/common/test_ints.py::test_int64_overflow (c engine param), test_int64_uint64_range, test_outside_int64_uint64_range, and the new test_outside_int64_uint64_range_follow_str, after applying the developer's test_ints.py diff to the buggy checkout
strategy.success_criterion: Transition: on the buggy revision (25607882c53f with the test diff applied) test_int64_overflow[c] and test_outside_int64_uint64_range[c] (and test_int64_uint64_range[c]) FAIL because the C engine returns strings where the test expects Python integers or object values; on the fixed revision (the PR merge commit with the same diff) these same tests PASS. test_outside_int64_uint64_range_follow_str is expected to PASS on both revisions, since the string-column behaviour it guards is unchanged; it is a regression guard, not the transition. The python engine cases are xfail-marked by the diff and should not count toward the transition.
strategy.numerical_probe: read_csv(StringIO('13007854817840017028824'), header=None, engine='c') should return int-valued object (exact Python int) on the fixed build and a str on the buggy build

input_output_examples.input: read_csv with engine='c' on a column containing 00013007854817840017028824 (ID column of test_int64_overflow)
read_csv with engine='c' on a column containing 13007854817840017963235
input_output_examples.buggy_output: the value is returned as a string

input_output_examples.input: read_csv with engine='c' on input f"{val}\nabc" where val = np.iinfo(np.uint64).max + 1
input_output_examples.buggy_output: string column with str(val) and 'abc' (passes on buggy as well)
input_output_examples.expected_output: DataFrame([str(val), 'abc']): column stays as strings with str(val)

risks: The buggy-to-fixed transition only exists in the C tokenizer/parser path; the pyarrow engine parses to float64 and is xfail-marked, and the python engine is also xfail-marked, so only the c engine carries the transition. If pyarrow is installed it will report xfail or skip, which is expected and not a failure.

Building the .pyx extensions requires a working C compiler and meson toolchain; on macOS arm64 or Windows the build may need extra setup, and the behaviour was not stated to be platform-specific, so the Linux x86_64 build is the safe choice.

The buggy revision's string expectations for in-range values (test_int64_uint64_range) are inferred from the diff comments, not from captured output; exact buggy output strings beyond the leading-zero example are not stated in the evidence.

Python version, NumPy version and Cython version are not stated as documented constraints; choices are era-inferred from the checked-out pyproject.toml and must be recorded. A mismatch with NumPy 2.x object construction could change exact object-dtype behaviour.
Editable build caches: after switching between buggy and fixed checkouts the meson rebuild must run, otherwise the stale extension will make the buggy and fixed results indistinguishable.
The PR body notes uncertainty about whether the behaviour change is desired; if the fixed revision differs from the PR merge in other ways, the transition may not hold.

oracle.why: Integers are compared exactly via tm.assert_frame_equal; the expected values are Python ints (e.g. 13007854817840017028824), so no tolerance applies.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: test_int64_overflow[c] and test_outside_int64_uint64_range[c] fail on the buggy revision because the C engine returns the big integers as strings, while the test's expected DataFrame holds integer (object) values, so assert_frame_equal reports a dtype/value mismatch. test_outside_int64_uint64_range_follow_str does not fail on buggy, since buggy already returns a string column there.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the C engine parses overflowing integers via PyLong_FromString in _try_pylong, so the c-engine integer expectations match exactly and all c-engine cases pass; the follow_str test passes on both revisions.
